quote: Gesucht wird eine Funktion $\xi(x)$ von solcher Beschaffenheit dass die Differenzial-Gleichung $\frac{dx'}{dt} = \xi(x')$ ($x'=x$ für $t=0$) bei geeigneter Wahl von $t$ grade ergiebt $x' = f(x)$. (Problem von Engel.)
english: Given a power series x' = f(x) = a_0 + a_1 x + ..., a function ξ(x) is sought such that the differential equation dx'/dt = ξ(x') (with x' = x for t = 0), for a suitable choice of t, yields exactly x' = f(x). (Problem of Engel.)
topic: Notes on proving that sin(1/x) can be expanded in a Fourier series, on an integral domain of expressions a_1 b_1^x + a_2 b_2^x + ... (after Hurwitz), on Gauss's early idea of non-Euclidean space, and on Engel's problem of finding a function whose differential equation flow yields a given power series map.

triage.modern_statement: This is the embedding problem for a one-dimensional map: when does a map lie in the flow of a vector field? It is also called continuous or fractional iteration, or finding the iterative logarithm. Take a local analytic map (germ) or a formal power series f(x) = a_0 + a_1 x + .... Does there exist ξ(x) such that the flow φ_t of the autonomous ODE dx/dt = ξ(x), with φ_0 = id, satisfies φ_{t0} = f for some time t0? If so, f is the time-t0 map of a one-parameter group of transformations, the vector field ξ is its infinitesimal generator, and ξ must satisfy Julia's equation ξ(f(x)) = f'(x) ξ(x). The problem can be asked formally, analytically, or for C^∞ maps. It is usually studied near a fixed point, where the behaviour depends on the multiplier f'(0).
triage.answered_by: There is no single solver. The answer came out of iteration theory and the local dynamics of germs over the 20th century. In the analytic case the answer is generally no. In 1960 Erdős and Jabotinsky ('On analytic iteration', J. Analyse Math. 8) noted that I. N. Baker had shown e^z − 1 has no analytic fractional iteration, so in general no analytic ξ exists. Baker went on to study fractional iteration and non-embeddable functions with multiplier 1 (J. Aust. Math. Soc. 1962 and 1964; Math. Z. 99, 1967). The modern account of the parabolic case relies on Écalle's resurgence theory and the Écalle–Voronin analytic classification. A germ conjugate to its normal form embeds in the conjugated flow, so embeddability depends on the germ's analytic invariants. Embedding results for smooth (C^∞) germs, including in higher dimensions, are still being refined.

evidence.claim: In 'On analytic iteration' (1960), Erdős and Jabotinsky state that I. N. Baker showed e^z − 1 has no analytic fractional iteration. For non-integer heights, the formal fractional-iterate series has radius of convergence zero. So in general no analytic generator exists, which answers Engel's question negatively in the analytic case.
Bibliographic details for Erdős and Jabotinsky, 'On analytic iteration', Journal d'Analyse Mathématique 8 (1960), 361–376.

I. N. Baker's papers on the subject: 'Permutable power series and regular iteration' (J. Aust. Math. Soc. 1962), 'Fractional iteration near a fixpoint of multiplier 1' (J. Aust. Math. Soc. 1964) and 'Non-embeddable functions with a fixpoint of multiplier 1' (Math. Z. 99, 1967). They are cited in a 2024 arXiv paper on iterates of power series.

In current work on parabolic germs, a holomorphic germ conjugate to its normal form, g = h∘v^1∘h^{-1}, embeds in the flow g_t = h∘v^t∘h^{-1}. The paper proves an 'Embedding in a flow' theorem tied to the analytic modulus.
Recent work relates the existence of a (formal) Fatou coordinate to embedding a germ in a (formal) one-parameter flow.
Embedding germs of smooth diffeomorphisms in flows, and the related functional equation for embedding interval homeomorphisms, are still being studied, including in higher dimensions.
A result for C^∞ hyperbolic germs F(x) = Ax + f(x) in R^n: if A has a real logarithm and its eigenvalues are weakly nonresonant, then F embeds in the flow of a C^∞ autonomous system.

Écalle's resurgence theory treats non-degenerate parabolic germs, including the iterative residue ('résidu itératif'). This is the modern framework for the obstruction to an analytic iterative logarithm.

triage.why: Hilbert's note describes the embedding-in-a-flow (iterative logarithm) problem: f must be the time-t map of dx'/dt = ξ(x'). 'Engel' is very likely Friedrich Engel, Lie's collaborator, since the problem asks whether a given transformation belongs to a one-parameter group. I did not find a source confirming this attribution or a specific Engel paper. The problem is not among Hilbert's 23 problems or the 24th. It has been answered in the sense that the conditions for an embedding to exist are now understood, and no single person solved it. In the analytic case an embedding generally fails to exist, as Baker showed for e^z − 1 (reported by Erdős and Jabotinsky in 1960), and Baker continued this work in the 1960s. Écalle–Voronin theory explains the parabolic case: embeddability depends on the germ's analytic invariants. Research on this continues for parabolic, Dulac, antiholomorphic and smooth germs. Not confirmed by my searches, though standard: if 0 < |a_1| ≠ 1, Koenigs linearization gives an analytic embedding; formal embeddings exist in general but usually diverge. Confidence is medium for three reasons. I could not verify Engel's original formulation or find a source that ties Hilbert's note to this literature. The 'solved' verdict is a broad reading, because the full answer comes from a body of work rather than one theorem. My searches stopped early at the tool limit.
